## discard-binding

Blocks **3** cards.

- **(op)** a discard whose count is chosen by the discarding player at resolution -- any number from 0 up to their hand size -- rather than a number the card fixes in advance; i.e. `discard` accepting a variable size (a `count: "any"`/`up_to` form, or an `objects` selector with `optional`) and asking the player which cards, not how many the card said
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `discard` in `ops` reads only `amount`, `random` and `player`: `op_discard` evaluates `amount` to an integer, sets `take = min(amount, len(hand))` and calls `ask_objects(ctx, "Discard", hand, take, take, ...)` with the same number as both floor and ceiling, so the player is forced to pitch exactly that many and can never choose zero or their whole hand. No value in `value_keys` can stand in, because the number is a decision, not a board fact -- `cards_in_hand` would make it a mandatory full discard. `may` wrapping `discard: 1` gives "you may discard a card", a different sentence. `repeat`'s `amount` is likewise a value, not a prompt, so it cannot loop until the player stops. The cost-side `discard_selector`/`discard` in `cost_keys` are payments for an activated ability and cannot be an effect of a triggered ability
- **(value)** a value naming how many cards that discard just discarded, so the follow-up draw can be "that many cards plus one" -- the discard needs to publish its count as a binding (the way `clash` writes one) that a later `draw` amount can read and add 1 to
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `discard` returns nothing and writes no binding, and every existing near-value is wrong for the same reasons `connive` is documented as an op rather than draw+discard+add_counters: `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` is `ledger.cards_to_graveyard`, a single integer across every graveyard at the table including earlier discards this turn; `count` over your graveyard counts what was already there (2 cards in the sandbox alone); `cards_in_hand` read after the discard is the rest of the hand, not what left it. All three load and all three draw a number nobody would recognise as wrong
- **(op)** an `up_to` (or optional-count) form of the `discard` op, letting the discarding player choose any number from zero to N -- "discard up to two cards" must be satisfiable with 0, 1 or 2 cards, chosen by the player as the effect resolves
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `op_discard` evaluates `amount` to a single number and calls `ask_objects(..., take, take, ...)` with the same value as both floor and ceiling, so the count is always exact and never declinable. The `optional` key in `selector_keys` is a *target* modifier and `discard` takes no target spec; `up_to` exists in the codebase only on `choose_mode` bounds and on `TargetSpec`, neither of which reaches a discard count
- **(value)** a value leaf reading how many cards the *immediately preceding discard in this same resolution* actually put into the graveyard, so "then draw that many cards" can be written as the `amount` of a following `draw`. The `as`-binding shape `exile`, `sacrifice` and `reveal` already use (record the chosen objects, read them back with `{"count": {"binding": ...}}`) is the obvious road: give `discard` an `as` and the value follows for free
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `discard` writes no binding at all, so nothing downstream can name what it took. The nearest `value_keys` entry, `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn`, is a turn-wide integer counting every card that reached any graveyard this turn -- creatures dying, spells resolving, other discards -- so it is a different number in every game state but the empty one. `cards_in_hand` measured before and after cannot be subtracted: there is no arithmetic over two snapshots of a value, only `minus` over two leaves evaluated at the same instant
- **(value)** a condition/value leaf that names the cards discarded during this ability's own resolution and filters them by card type, so an `if` can ask "was a creature card discarded this way" and "was a noncreature card discarded this way" — e.g. a `discarded_this_way` value taking a selector and returning a count, usable inside `cmp`/`exists`, populated by the `discard` op for the duration of the resolution (and across a `for_each_player` loop, since this card asks about every player's discard, not just the controller's)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `discard` records nothing and returns nothing. `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` is the closest value key and is wrong twice over: it is turn-scoped rather than resolution-scoped and it counts every graveyard at the table and every earlier discard, mill or death this turn. `count` over `{"zone": "graveyard"}` counts what was already there — in the verification sandbox that is two creature cards, so the creature branch would fire unconditionally. `connive` is the only op that reads its own discard, but it is a fused draw+discard+counter-on-self op with "nonland" hardcoded; it cannot gate an arbitrary effect, cannot ask about "creature" vs "noncreature", and cannot see another player's discard. Its own docstring states the case: "the cards that were just discarded, which nothing in the condition or value language can name".

## cast-from-graveyard

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(static_effect)** a static ability that grants its controller permission to cast *other* cards from their own graveyard, with a filter naming which cards qualify (here `types: ["Creature"]`) -- the Muldrotha/Karador/Gisa and Geralf shape
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `play_lands_from_graveyard` is the only graveyard-casting permission in `static_effects`, and it is hard-wired to the land drop: `legality.py` reads it through `player_plays_lands_from_graveyard` solely to widen the land-play action, so it can neither be pointed at creature spells nor at casting at all. The `cast_from_graveyard` in `condition_keys` is not a permission -- it reads the `cast_from_graveyard` flag the stack sets on a spell, and the loader refuses it on any card without its own `flashback`, so it only ever asks about the source card itself, never about other cards in the yard
- **(engine)** a per-turn use limit on such a casting permission -- "Once during each of your turns" must let exactly one qualifying spell be cast per turn of the permission's controller, and the used-up state must reset each turn
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `set_turn_flag`/`has_turn_flag` can record that something happened this turn, but they are effect ops and conditions readable only while an ability resolves; nothing consults them when legality enumerates castable spells, so there is no way to make a standing permission stop offering itself after its first use
- **(static_effect)** a static ability on one permanent that lets its controller cast OTHER cards from their graveyard, filtered by card type (here artifact spells) and rate-limited to once during each of that player's turns
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `play_lands_from_graveyard` is the only graveyard-play permission in `static_effects`, and legality.py reads it solely through `player_plays_lands_from_graveyard` for the land drop -- it cannot authorize a spell cast, cannot be narrowed by type, and carries no per-turn counter. Flashback is the only other graveyard cast route and it is a property of the card being cast (`card.flashback`, read off the card in legality.py), so it cannot be conferred on arbitrary artifact cards by a different permanent.
- **(replacement)** an enters-tapped replacement applied to a DIFFERENT permanent than the ability's source -- the artifact that was cast from the graveyard under this permission -- conditioned on that permanent having been cast this way
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The only enters-tapped replacement is `self_enters_tapped` (zones.py), which fires on the source's own entry; the free tier mis-templated this clause onto Edgar himself, which is not what the card says. The `cast_from_graveyard` CONDITION key exists but only reads `obj.cast_from_graveyard` during a resolution -- there is no replacement event keyed on a permanent entering that was cast from a graveyard.

## graveyard-movement-ledger

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(selector)** a selector key over graveyard cards that matches only those put there this turn, and that can further restrict which zone they came from ("from anywhere other than the battlefield") -- i.e. the engine must remember, per card now in a graveyard, the turn it arrived and the zone it arrived from
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` is the only this-turn graveyard fact the engine keeps, and `values.py` returns `ledger.cards_to_graveyard`, a bare integer across all graveyards -- it retains neither which cards arrived nor where they came from. No key in `selector_keys` reads arrival time or previous zone, so a graveyard selector can only see the whole yard, which would let this ability recur a creature that died in combat five turns ago
- **(engine)** a per-turn ledger of cards that left a player's graveyard this turn (to any zone -- exile, hand, library, battlefield), exposed both as a condition an intervening-if can ask ("if a card left your graveyard this turn") and as a count value, keyed by the graveyard's owner
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: value_keys has `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn`, which counts movement in the opposite direction (cards put *into* the graveyard) and so is true in exactly the wrong cases. `cast_from_graveyard` only asks about the source spell itself, not about any card. `has_turn_flag` reads a flag written by `set_turn_flag` on the same source, so it cannot observe a zone change caused by some other card. `exists`/`zone_is`/`cmp` only read the graveyard's current contents, which says nothing about what departed it. The engine keeps only `cards_drawn_this_turn`, `resolutions_this_turn` and `triggers_this_turn` as per-turn ledgers -- no graveyard-departure tracking exists to read.

## leaves-graveyard

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(trigger_event)** a trigger event fired when one or more cards leave a specified player's graveyard, batched so that a single move of several cards fires the ability once, and filterable by the leaving cards' printed characteristics (here: creature cards, your graveyard)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: trigger_events has 'leaves_battlefield' and 'dies', which watch the battlefield and fire on cards arriving in a graveyard rather than departing it; 'discard' and 'sacrificed' likewise only ever put cards *into* a graveyard. Nothing in the list observes the graveyard as a source zone, so the many ways a card leaves it -- reanimation via return_from_graveyard or put_onto_battlefield, exile via the exile op or an exile_from_graveyard cost, a graveyard cast, a shuffle-back -- all happen unobserved. The batching ('one or more ... leave') is a second requirement no existing event carries: every listed event fires per object.
- **(trigger_event)** a triggered-ability event that fires when one or more cards move out of a graveyard -- a DSL trigger name mapping to a graveyard-departure event that carries the owner of the graveyard (so `controller: "you"` can restrict it to your own) and batches every card that left as part of the same move into a single firing, so exiling three cards from your graveyard for one cost puts one +1/+1 counter on this creature and not three
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `trigger_events` carries `leaves_battlefield` (and `dies`, `sacrificed`), all of which are about a permanent leaving the battlefield -- the wrong zone entirely, and a card leaving the graveyard is never a permanent leaving play. `exile_from_graveyard` is a *cost* key and `return_from_graveyard` is an *op*: they are two of the ways a card leaves a graveyard, not a way to notice one, and hanging the counter off either would only cover a card's own effects, never an opponent's graveyard hate, another player's reanimation of your creature, or a flashback/escape cast that exiles on resolution. The engine's `ZONE_CHANGE` event (src/automtg/engine/events.py) does carry `from`/`to` zones and would be the natural substrate, but it is absent from `TRIGGER_EVENTS` in src/automtg/engine/triggers.py, so no DSL trigger can listen to it, and even if one could, it is emitted once per object moved, which is exactly the per-card firing the printed "one or more" forbids.

## additional-cost-on-alternative-cast

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a card-level `additional_cost` that is charged on every way of casting the spell, not only from hand -- specifically on the flashback (and other alternative-cost / non-hand) cast lines, so that a mandatory additional cost is owed by the graveyard cast too (601.2f)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `additional_cost` is the right slot and `cost_keys.discard` is the right price, but legality only offers additional-cost cast variants under `state.objects[oid].zone is Zone.HAND`, and the flashback line is built by calling `_cast_variant(..., flashback=True)` directly from the graveyard loop, bypassing the `_cast_options` block that sets `additional_times`. `game._cast` pays the non-mana half only when `action.additional_times` is nonzero, so a flashed-back Laughing Mad would cost {3}{R} and discard nothing -- a strictly-better free draw-two, which is exactly the quiet wrongness the printed reminder 'and any additional costs' rules out. Moving the discard into `spell_effects` as the `discard` op is not a substitute: that pays at resolution rather than as a cost, and lets the spell be cast when the price could not be paid.

## alternative-cost-pay-life

Blocks **1** card.

- **(replacement)** An alternative cost that REPLACES a spell's mana cost with a life payment computed from that spell's own mana value, applied automatically to every spell cast under the permission above. Needs (a) alternative-cost machinery that substitutes for the whole mana cost rather than reducing it, (b) the substituted cost to be paid in life, and (c) its amount to be read from the spell being cast (its mana value), not from the source granting the permission. The life payment is a cost, so a player who cannot pay that much life cannot cast the spell that way.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `pay_life` exists in `cost_keys`, but `cost_keys` is only what an ACTIVATED ABILITY'S OWN cost may contain -- it cannot be attached to some other spell being cast from a zone. `spell_cost_reduction` in `static_effects` is the only static that touches what other spells cost, and it reduces a mana cost by an amount; it cannot swap the payment to a different resource, and reducing to {0} would be a different card (it would not drain the caster's life, so Citadel's self-limiting downside would vanish). Nothing in `static_effects` or `condition_keys` can read the mana value of the spell currently being cast at payment time; `mana_value_of` is a `value_key` for effects at resolution, not a payment-time hook.

  - If you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than pay its mana cost.

</details>

## become-copy

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** an op that makes an existing permanent already on the battlefield become a copy of another permanent (layer 1 copy effect), with a duration (until end of turn as well as permanently) and an `except_` override block so the copy can keep its own name -- e.g. {"op": "become_copy", "objects": {"self_only": true}, "copying": {"target": "creature"}, "duration": "end_of_turn", "except_": {"name": "Gogo, Mysterious Mime"}}
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `copy_permanent` is the only copy op for permanents and it always calls `create_token` with the source's def_id -- it makes a NEW token copy and never alters the object it is pointed at, so it cannot turn Gogo itself into a copy, and it has no duration at all. `animate` overwrites power/toughness, colors, types and keywords with literal values, so it cannot take another object's whole printed characteristics, and `transform` only flips a double-faced card to its own back face. Making a token instead would leave the real Gogo unchanged and add a permanent the card never creates.
- **(engine)** a copy effect applied in place must re-derive the target permanent's characteristics from the copied CardDef while leaving counters, damage, attachments and status on the object, and must expire cleanly at end of turn, restoring Gogo's printed characteristics
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The object model derives identity from a fixed `def_id` set when the object is created (`copy_permanent` relies on exactly that), and there is no continuous-effect layer that rewrites an existing object's def_id for a duration; `lose_all_abilities` and `set_pt` are the only statics that overwrite characteristics and neither can source them from another object.

## cast-this-way

- **(selector)** A selector key that names exactly the cards a free-cast op (`play_exiled`) actually cast during this resolution -- e.g. `{"cast_this_way": "self"}` -- so a following `for_each` can loop them and a `lose_life` inside can use the existing `{"owner_of": "each"}` player spec with `{"mana_value_of": {"binding": "each"}}` as its amount.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `play_exiled` chooses its cards, calls `cast_for_free` on each and binds nothing, so no later effect can see which ones were taken. The closest selector is `exiled_with: "self"`, which is the wrong set in both directions at once: a card that was cast has left exile and no longer matches, and a card the player declined to cast still does -- so it names 'exiled this way' and never 'cast this way'. `was_cast` is a condition about the ability's own source, not a pool, and `snapshot` captures one object chosen in advance rather than an unknown-size set decided mid-resolution.

</details>

## choose-permanents

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** an op that has a named chooser pick permanents out of a pool and records them as a binding without doing anything to them -- here the spell's controller picking survivors on another player's battlefield, so a later `sacrifice` can spare them with `exclude_binding`
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Every op that writes a binding via `as` also acts on what it picked: `sacrifice`, `exile`, `gain_control`, `reveal`, `create_token`, `copy_permanent`, `search_zones`. `snapshot` writes a binding without acting, but it takes `oids[0]` of its pool with no `count`/`chooser` narrowing at all, so it cannot be a choice and cannot hold four picks. There is no way to mark the four kept permanents before the mass sacrifice, and inverting the card into 'choose the ones to sacrifice' is a different choice -- the printed card names one survivor per type, not an all-but-one selection.
- **(selector)** a per-type quota on a single choice: 'at most one artifact, at most one creature, at most one enchantment and at most one planeswalker', each skipped when that player controls none, with a permanent that is two of those types eligible as either
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `count` is one flat number applied to a pool that `types`/`any_types` filter uniformly, so `{"any_types": ["Artifact","Creature","Enchantment","Planeswalker"], "count": 4}` would happily take four creatures. Splitting it into four separate one-of-each-type choices is not a workaround either: `exclude_binding` reads a single binding name, and every binding write assigns the name outright rather than appending, so the one `sacrifice` that follows can spare only the last of the four.

  - Then each player sacrifices all other nonland permanents they control.

</details>

## entered-from-graveyard

Blocks **1** card.

- **(trigger_event)** an enters trigger that can ask which zone the entering permanent came from -- "if one or more of them entered from a graveyard" -- covering every route out of the yard (reanimation, `put_onto_battlefield` from a graveyard, `return_from_graveyard`), plus the ability to read the entering object's own cast-from-a-graveyard flag for the "or was cast from a graveyard" half. Needs the origin zone on the ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD payload and a positive filter/condition over it that is evaluated about the *triggering* object
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `zones._enter_battlefield` fires ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD with `player`, `source`, `oid`, `card`, `was_creature` and `cause` only -- the origin zone is put on the separate ZONE_CHANGE event as `from`, and no trigger event maps to ZONE_CHANGE. `cause` names the mechanism (`put_onto_battlefield`, `manifest`, `meld`), not the zone, and the only clause that reads it is `not_cause`, a single cause to *refuse*; there is no positive cause match, and matching on causes would in any case miss a reanimation and catch a battlefield-to-battlefield blink. In `condition_keys`, `zone_is` reports the source's *current* zone (`obj.zone.value`), `was_cast` is restricted by `WAS_CAST_TRIGGERS` to `self_enters` because it answers about the ability's own permanent, and `cast_from_graveyard` reads `obj.cast_from_graveyard` off the ability's source and is refused by the loader on any card without its own `flashback` -- so none of the three can be pointed at the creature that just entered. `static_filter_keys` and `selector_keys` have no origin-zone or arrival-history key either

Concretely: something like an `as` binding on `may` that accumulates the accepting player ids across the loop, readable afterwards as `{"players": {"binding": "accepted"}}` on `damage`. The first half of the sentence ("Each player may discard their hand and draw five cards") is already expressible as `for_each_player` over `each_player` wrapping a `may` whose `player` is `{"binding": "each_player"}` with `discard` + `draw`; only the back-reference is blocked.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `set_flag`/`has_flag` is the closest recording mechanism and is object-scoped, not player-scoped: `op_set_flag` writes into `obj.flags` of battlefield objects only, and the `has_flag` condition is always asked of `ctx.source_oid`, the ability's own source -- so it cannot say anything about a player. `set_turn_flag`/`has_turn_flag` is the same shape keyed by oid. `for_each_player` does bind `each_player`, but the binding is overwritten on every iteration and restored at the end of the loop, so nothing survives to be read after the loop. `join_forces` is the only op that accumulates across a player loop and it accumulates an integer total, not the set of seats that said yes. Folding the `damage` into the `may`'s own `effects` is the tempting near miss and is wrong in two visible ways: it damages each opponent before the next opponent has been asked (in multiplayer a player can be killed mid-loop, changing later choices), and it splits one simultaneous damage event into several separate ones, which is observable to damage triggers and to prevention shields.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Snort** (rank 5124) — `snort`
  - Each player may discard their hand and draw five cards. Then Snort deals 5 damage to each opponent who discarded their hand this way.

</details>

## prepared

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a per-permanent 'prepared' state that is itself a standing casting permission: while a permanent you control is prepared, you may cast a copy of that card's *other castable face* (here the {1}{B} sorcery half of a Creature // Sorcery card) from the battlefield, paying that face's own cost at that face's own timing, with the permanent staying on the battlefield, and the act of casting it clearing the state
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Every piece the engine has is one step off. `second_face`/`second_face_zone` already model a second castable face, but the zone is `Literal["hand", "graveyard"]` -- split and Adventure halves cast from hand, Aftermath from the graveyard -- and there is no battlefield option, which is the only zone prepared ever casts from. `cast_copy` is an *effect op*: it runs during a resolution somebody else started, copies the ability's own source card, and puts the copy on the stack for free via `put_copy_on_stack`; prepared is instead a player-initiated cast of the other face at its printed cost, offered every time the player has priority at sorcery speed, so it belongs to the legal-actions enumerator and not to any op. `play_exiled`/`cast_for_free` is the nearest cast permission and is wrong twice over: it casts one specific card out of exile without paying, not a copy of a face of a permanent on the battlefield for its cost. The static permissions are all lands (`play_lands_from_graveyard`, `play_lands_from_library_top`); none of them offers a spell, and none is scoped to a face of the permanent it sits on
- **(op)** an effect that turns the prepared state on -- 'this creature becomes prepared' from a triggered ability, and 'this creature enters prepared' as an enters-with characteristic in the same slot enters-tapped occupies -- plus the matching turn-off used when the copy is cast ('doing so unprepares it')
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `set_flag` writes an arbitrary word onto a permanent and `has_flag` reads it back, which is exactly how renown is stored, but a flag is inert bookkeeping: nothing in the casting-permission path consults `obj.flags`, so a permanent flagged 'prepared' would gain no ability to cast anything and the card would silently do nothing. `set_flag` is also one-way by design -- there is no clear/remove counterpart in `ops`, and `set_turn_flag` expires at the turn boundary rather than on use -- so even a flag-backed implementation could not express 'doing so unprepares it', which is what stops the copy being cast every turn for ever

</details>

## reflexive-trigger

  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: trigger_events has no reflexive/'when you do' event, and all of its entries are board events (self_enters, permanent_enters, dies, ...) fired by the game rather than by an earlier clause of the same spell. `delayed_trigger` and `delay` fire on a later step or turn and take no new targets, so neither can hand the player a target choice mid-resolution; and a card-level target spec is declared before the spell resolves, when the opponents' graveyards have not been exiled yet and there is nothing legal to point at.

## unearth

Blocks **1** card.

- **(replacement)** a self-scoped, duration-bounded replacement of a permanent's *leave-the-battlefield* zone change -- "if this permanent would leave the battlefield, exile it instead" -- that fires for every destination (graveyard, hand, exile, library, command zone), not only for a death, and that is installed by the resolving unearth ability on the card it just returned and lasts as long as that permanent is on the battlefield
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `replace_deaths` is the only op in `ops` that redirects a zone change, and `zones.move_object` gates it on `from_zone is BATTLEFIELD and to_zone is GRAVEYARD` (src/automtg/engine/zones.py:95-99) -- so it catches a death and nothing else. Unearth's clause is the *whole* leave-the-battlefield event: bounced to hand, exiled by removal, shuffled into the library, sent to the command zone. Substituting `replace_deaths` is not a rounding error on this card, it is the card's central loop: this Priest's own ability sacrifices itself, and the printed replacement is what makes that a one-way trip. Modelled as death-only, an opponent's bounce or exile still leaves a card that can be unearthed again; modelled not at all (the engine's currently documented unearth divergence, docs/rules-coverage.md line 99, which pairs a `put_onto_battlefield` of `self_only` with `grant_keyword` haste and a `delay`ed `exile`), the sacrifice puts the Priest straight back in the graveyard to be unearthed again next turn, making it an unbounded reanimation engine the printed card explicitly forbids. `delay` cannot say it either: a delayed trigger fires at a named step, and this has to fire the moment the permanent would move, before it lands anywhere. `until_leaves` is the opposite link -- it declares a return, not an interception -- and `static_effects` carries only `replace_token_creation`, which docs/rules-coverage.md line 182 states is deliberately not the start of a general replacement system.
